name: addpipe16_carryselect4_tree
rationale: All four prior hand-built full-width prefix/tree/CLA/8-8-split adders underperformed the plain '+' baseline, suggesting ABC maps a native 16-bit '+' very efficiently and that deep bit-level restructuring or wide flat mux-chains hurts. This design instead builds a genuine hierarchical (radix-4) carry-select adder: four independent 4-bit blocks are each added twice via native '+' (assuming cin=0 and cin=1, fully parallel, no cross dependency), then combined with only TWO levels of small 4-bit-wide selects (4+4 -> 8, then 8+8 -> 16) instead of four bit-level merge stages (Kogge-Stone) or four levels of 1-bit hypothesis muxes (prior conditional-sum attempt). Using native '+' for the small 4-bit leaves lets Yosys/ABC apply its favorable $add technology mapping at the block level, while the shallow 2-level select tree should give a shorter critical path than a monolithic 16-bit ripple/CLA chain and than the previously-tried flat 8/8 carry-select (whose single big 8-bit adders and single mux level scored below baseline). This is a structurally new point (fine leaf granularity + genuine binary merge tree) not yet attempted, offering a plausible path to a new WNS/area trade-off.
